# FormGroup accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:start -->

FormGroup arranges a set of checkboxes or switches. It renders a `div` with no role. The group semantics come from a `fieldset` with a legend, or from `role="group"` with a name. For radio buttons, use RadioGroup.

FormGroup rates layout criteria (1.3.2, 1.4.10, 2.4.3) because it sets the layout, and group criteria (1.3.1, 2.4.6, 3.3.2) because `role="group"` makes it the named group element.

<!-- intro:end -->

## Known gaps

None.

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- FormGroup shows its controls in DOM order, in a column, or in a row with `row`. It does not reverse the order.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Read a FormGroup with `row` with the reading keys (<kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> in NVDA, <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> in VoiceOver).
3. Compare the reading order with the visual order.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->the reading order matches the visual order.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- Instructions for a group must not rely on its position or color alone. This is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that refers to a group of options.
2. Make sure that it names the group by its label.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->each instruction names the group by its label.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The legend or the `aria-labelledby` element names the group. Whether the name describes the group is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the name of each group.
2. Read each name without its options.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->each group name tells the purpose of the set, for example "Toppings".<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormGroup.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- FormGroup renders a `div` with no role, so by itself it does not tell assistive technology that the controls form a group.
- With `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` on FormGroup, FormGroup itself is a named group. A unit test confirms that FormGroup passes these attributes to its root element.
- No docs page or demo documents `role="group"` on FormGroup. The docs show only the `fieldset` pattern, in CheckboxesGroup and SwitchesGroup. A follow-up must document the `role="group"` pattern.
- Inside `FormControl component="fieldset"` with `FormLabel component="legend"`, the `fieldset` is the group, and the legend is its name. FormGroup adds nothing to this pattern.
- A group without a `fieldset` or a role has no name. This is the author's responsibility.
- FormControl does not connect a FormHelperText to the group. The author adds `aria-describedby`. In the error state, the checkboxes get no `aria-invalid`, because Checkbox and Switch take only `disabled` from FormControl.
- ARIA does not allow `aria-label` on an element with no role, and assistive technology can ignore it. The FormControlLabelPosition docs demos use this pattern. axe-core `aria-prohibited-attr` reports it only as `incomplete`, and no fixture exercises it.
- In the ScrollPlayground Popper demo, each FormGroup starts with a Typography heading (`h6`), for example "Prevent Overflow". No `fieldset` or `aria-labelledby` connects the heading to the group, so the group has no name. This is a demo issue.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari). In Safari, turn on "Press Tab to highlight each item".
2. In a FormGroup inside `FormControl component="fieldset"` with a legend, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into the group.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Do the test again with a FormGroup that has no `fieldset`.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader announces the group name once when focus enters the group.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `form-field-multiple-labels` ✅

<!-- 3.3.2:start -->

- The legend, or the element that `aria-labelledby` names, is the visible label of the group. FormGroup adds no label of its own.
- The required state of a group is a FormLabel gap. The [FormLabel report](../FormLabel/accessibility.md) rates it under 1.3.1.
- Result from the checkbox, switch, app bar, list, focus-visible, Popper, and CRUD dashboard demos:
  - CheckboxesGroup, SwitchesGroup, both FormControlLabelPosition demos, and FocusVisibleCustomIcons have a group label.
  - CheckboxLabels, SwitchLabels, CustomizedSwitches, MenuAppBar, InteractiveList, and FullFocusVisibleDemo have no group label. Their controls are separate options, and each control has its own label. In FullFocusVisibleDemo, the "Checkbox" text next to the group is a row caption of the showcase, not a group label.
  - EmployeeForm, in the CRUD dashboard template, uses FormGroup as a layout wrapper for the whole form. Each field has its own label.
  - ScrollPlayground shows a visible heading above each group. The heading is not connected to the group. See 1.3.1.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Check that each checkbox and switch group that asks one question has a visible label.
2. Check that the instructions say how many options the user must select.

<!-- 3.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.3.2:pass:start -->each group that asks one question has a visible label and clear instructions.<!-- 3.3.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- The group has `flex-wrap: wrap`, so a row of controls wraps onto more lines. A Playwright test confirms that a row of five checkboxes does not scroll horizontally at 320 CSS px.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

#### 2.4.3 Focus Order · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormGroup.test.js`

<!-- 2.4.3:start -->

- The controls are tab stops in DOM order, also with `row`. A test in a real browser confirms that a row group shows its controls from left to right in tab order.

<!-- 2.4.3:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A).** <!-- 1.1.1:start -->FormGroup renders no content of its own.<!-- 1.1.1:end -->
- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.1 Use of Color (A).** <!-- 1.4.1:start -->FormGroup renders no color of its own. It gets the `error` class in the error state, but no error style. The legend and the helper text show the error color.<!-- 1.4.1:end -->
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA), 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA), 1.4.5 Images of Text (AA), 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA).** <!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:start -->FormGroup renders no text of its own. The legend and the labels own these criteria.<!-- 1.4.3,1.4.4,1.4.5,1.4.12:end -->
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA).** <!-- 1.4.11:start -->FormGroup renders no graphical object and no component boundary.<!-- 1.4.11:end -->
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA), 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (A), 2.5.3 Label in Name (A), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA), 3.2.1 On Focus (A), 3.2.2 On Input (A), 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA).** <!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.7,2.4.11,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.1,3.2.2,3.2.4:start -->FormGroup is not focusable and has no action of its own. The controls inside it cover these.<!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.7,2.4.11,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.1,3.2.2,3.2.4:end -->
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** The component renders no links.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A).** <!-- 4.1.2:start -->FormGroup sets no role, and its own markup supplies no name. The group role and name pattern is rated under 1.3.1.<!-- 4.1.2:end -->
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** Emits no status messages; state changes are covered by 4.1.2.

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
